question_decisions.note: Confirmed. A pedigree showing devolution of title must state the legal effect of the Final Decree in Partition Case No 2525/P and of Deed of Gift No 925 with its reserved life interest. Searching the corpus for a partition statute returns nothing, and grep for 'life interest' and 'usufruct' returns only Land Reform Law ceiling provisions and Registration of Title Act s.46. The only gift statute in the corpus is 5-2017 on revocation for gross ingratitude, which no fact engages. s.36 remits those silences to Roman-Dutch law, so the reserve is right.

Kept as proposed_gold. Every fraction was recomputed independently from the corpus text and agrees: Kapila's death in 2011 gives Champa 1/2 (s.22) and each of four children 1/8 (s.24); Anusha's death in 2012 gives Hasitha 1/16 (s.22) and 1/48 to each of three paternal half-sisters (ss.26, 29, 30); Prema's death in 2015 gives Champa 7/96 (s.25) and 7/192 to each of Rupa and Seetha (ss.25, 30). Totals: Champa 110/192, Rupa 35/192, Seetha 35/192, Hasitha 12/192 = 192/192. Two claims are marked disputed and the ownership premise is recorded as a disagreement, but neither defeats the statutory computation.

disagreements.researcher_position: Q01 is reserved because the deed-of-gift and life-interest link has no statutory support, while Q02 is statute_only because Kapila's ownership of the entirety is taken as a fact given in the background.
disagreements.verifier_position: The same non-statutory link sits under Q02. The answer's application asserts that Kapila held the entirety 'once his father's reserved life interest ended on Mahesh's death on 24 April 2008', and no corpus provision states that a reserved life interest determines on the life tenant's death. I accept the split, because that proposition reads as construction of the deed's own words ('absolute and irrevocable gift subject to life interest of the Donor') rather than a contested doctrine, and because Q02 asks only for shares among heirs. But the premise is load-bearing for every fraction and is carried by no answer_claim, so a lawyer should settle whether Q02 must also be reserved.

disagreements.researcher_position: The facts describe Anusha and Prema only as having died; the answer computes their estates under Part III and discloses the intestacy assumption in the conclusion.
disagreements.verifier_position: Confirmed as an assumption, not authority. The Wills Ordinance 21-1844 holds nothing that presumes intestacy, and s.22 by its terms bites only 'when any person shall die intestate'. Recorded as an added corpus gap. If either left a will the whole downstream computation changes.

unsupported_claims: CL-M023-Q02-001 marked disputed: it states that Part III 'applies to the estate of any person dying after its proclamation', which is only one limb of s.20. The section also requires the deceased to have been unmarried at death or, if married, married after the proclamation. Both limbs hold on these facts, so the outcome is unaffected, but the rule as stated is incomplete.

CL-M023-Q02-015 marked disputed: 'Malani and Mithila hold no share in Lot 1, because Mahesh had gifted the entirety to Kapila before his death' cites PROV-M023-005 (s.24, preferential right of children), which says nothing about property already disposed of by gift. The proposition rests on the background fact of Deed of Gift No 925 and on Roman-Dutch donation law outside the corpus, not on s.24.

The premise that Kapila held the entirety of Lot 1 from 24 April 2008 appears in gold_answer_draft.application but has no entry in answer_claims and no supporting provision, yet it is the starting point of every fraction. Recorded as a disagreement rather than rejected, because it is fact-derived.

lawyer_questions: Does Q02 survive as statute_only? Every fraction starts from Kapila holding the entirety of Lot 1 once the donor's reserved life interest fell in on 24 April 2008, and no provision in this corpus states that a reserved life interest determines on the life tenant's death. If that premise needs Roman-Dutch authority rather than construction of the deed, Q02 must be reserved alongside Q01.
Is the intestacy of Anusha (2012) and of Prema (2015) a safe assumption, given that the facts state only that each died and the corpus holds nothing that presumes intestacy?

For Anusha's estate, is it right that no grandparent or higher ascendant on Sandya's side survived her, so that s.29 lets the three paternal half-sisters take the whole 1/16 rather than one-half? Malani, the paternal grandmother, is on the same side as the half-sisters and does not trigger the exception; that reading is confirmed.
Should Hasitha Perera, the widower of a deceased co-owner, be listed among 'the heirs' in the answer to Q02, or does the examiner expect only the blood line?
